text: Code refactoring means improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The program should behave exactly the same before and after. The main goal is to make code easier to read and understand. When code is messy, developers often call it technical debt. Refactoring helps reduce this debt by cleaning up complex parts, removing repetition, and giving variables clearer names. It may take time, but it saves effort later. Teams that refactor regularly find it easier to add new features and fix bugs, because the code becomes simpler and more organised.
